The One Big Beautiful Bill Act forces accountability—something bureaucrats hate. Medicaid’s structural rot isn’t solved by endless federal cash infusions. Kentucky’s provider tax scheme exploited loopholes to inflate federal reimbursements, creating a shell game where taxpayers fund bureaucracy instead of care.

UofL Health’s canceled birthing center reflects state-level mismanagement, not federal cuts. Hospitals nationwide survive Medicaid adjustments when states prioritize efficiency over graft.

The bill doesn’t slash care for mothers/kids—it stops states from treating Medicaid like an ATM for bloated admin costs. Real reform requires trimming fat, not crying about imaginary closures.

See how the numbers expose the real drivers behind Medicaid waste: https://t.co/Oru2zTOvPt

The One Big, Beautiful Bill claims $1T in Medicaid "savings" by purging rolls and imposing work requirements—but slashing federal support forces states to cut services. UofL Health already axed a birthing center, blaming Medicaid rollbacks.
